fields.why: No design is named; the NIS-ACM telephone survey supports cross-sectional, and 'used to monitor' coverage with no targets supports surveillance/descriptive. Either alone or both is defensible.

Free vaccine, trusted messengers and 'equitable access' appear only as programmatic measures that 'might increase equitable access' (recommendations); the article names no determinant as the cause of the racial coverage disparity.

Every SPD claim ('higher than most other groups', 'lowest among uninsured', 'increased with age') falls under the blanket t-test statement, which v5 classes as per-group vs referent only; precedence puts it above side by side, so no separate side-by-side entry.
